primitives.name: Three-Down Advancement Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is a rule which says that in three attempts a side must advance the ball five or take it back twenty yards under penalty of surrendering it to the opponents.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D': 'number of downs', 'A': 'yards advanced per down', 'T': 'total required advancement in yards'}
primitives.assumptions: Each down is independent; failure results in possession change.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When total advancement < 5 yards after 3 downs.

layer2.mapping: GSE models down progression as a Markov chain; GSI infers strategic intent from down-state probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Turnover probability given current down and yardage

primitives.name: Scoring Event Mechanics
primitives.verbatim_quote: There are two ways in which points may be made: by kicking the ball, as above described, over the goal, and by touching it down behind the goal line.
primitives.assumptions: Only end zone actions result in score; punts excluded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ball crosses goal line without valid touchback or safety.

layer2.mapping: GSE encodes scoring as terminal state transitions; GSI evaluates likelihood of scoring paths.
layer2.telemetry: Probability of scoring given field position and time remaining
